name: North Creek
description:
SUNDAY 25 October

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED - Hard

DESCRIPTION
This will be a full day, creek based hike. We'll traverse across some rough country. There will be a waterfall rock face to climb up (exposed ledges that some may find challenging) and plenty of rock hopping, boulder scrambles and steep climbs.
This will be a hot but picturesque walk with the opportunity to have a swim to cool off.

We did this walk a few weeks ago at short notice (due to the weather elsewhere) and a few members missed out so we're heading there again. Last time we headed home via Cockatoo Creek but this time we'll take another route.

FITNESS
To be suitable for this walk, a good analogy would be doing a Castle Hill spur, without a track, three times with ease before lunchtime.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for full day eg minimum 4L or refill from the creek (treat or filter is recommended) and electrolytes
- Clothing: long sleeves and long pants/gaiters as we'll be heading through the scrub. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed and sturdy footwear
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.

COST
Non members = $5 walk fee for insurance
Must be over 18years to participate

WALK LEADER, INFO and REGISTRATION
Walk leader is Keith.
To discuss suitability, to register or for more information please contact tsvbush@hotmail.com and we will get back to you asap or contact him directly if you have his details. 

WALK DETAILS

Return time: estimated 4-5pm

name: Crystal Creek Falls (bottom) - pls read event description
description:
REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL.

SUMMARY: This will be a full day walk involving some on-track walking, off-track bush bashing, boulder hopping and steep declines/inclines. 
Expect jungle, vines, wait-awhile, a few boulders (there is a challenging boulder scramble near the bottom). At the bottom, we can admire the view of the bottom tier of Crystal Creek Falls (which you cannot see from the top), explore a bit and then we will try to get further downstream. This is largely the unknown exploratory bit, and may be very hard.

RATING: Hard - for experienced and fit bushwalkers only

WHAT TO BRING:
- Food and drink for the day
- Closed in footwear
- Long sleeve clothing recommended

name: Mt Marlow via Many Peaks track (Pallarenda)
description:
SUNDAY 18 OCTOBER 

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED: Easy to moderate - suitable for most walkers with reasonable fitness. The walk requires walking up hill on a track with some climbing and stepping over rocks and rough ground.

DESCRIPTION
The Many Peaks track leads up and along the Many Peaks Range to reach the summit of Mt Marlow. Great views are to be had of Town Common, Townsville City and out to the islands. Once we descend off Mt Marlow we'll return via the Lagoon Trail

For more information have a look at these resources:
** https://parks.des.qld.gov.au/parks/townsville/things-to-do#many_peaks_track
** https://wanderstories.space/cape-pallarenda/

Distance: approx 11km
Time: allow 4hrs

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for half day eg minimum 2L. It will be hot walking back along the Lagoon Trail
- Clothing: There is limited shade on Mt Marlow and the Lagoon Trail therefore sun safe clothing (ie long sleeve shirt, hat) is suggested.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent for mozzies
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.

COST

name: FULL - The Terraces and High Camp
description:
[EVENT FULL] SUNDAY 11 OCTOBER

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED: Mod -hard

DESCRIPTION
A club favourite walk up Palm Creek (St Margaret's Creek system) to the Terraces, Ultima Falls, Garden Wall, and High Camp.  The Terraces/High Camp features many waterfalls and is one of the most scenic creeks in the region (and the state) and one of our local gems.

This will be a full day creek based hike with sections that are off track cross country over rough terrain. It will involve rockhopping, boulder scrambles, rockface traverses, scrub and vines, uneven footing, slippery rocks and a couple of steep climbs. 

On way out, we'll stop at the at the Rockslides for a swim....
and most importantly, ice creams at the roadhouse on the way home to finish the day off. It will be a  good day out for our adventurous bushwalkers.

FITNESS
To be suitable for this walk, a good analogy would be doing a Castle Hill spur, without a track, two-three times with ease before lunchtime.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for full day eg minimum 2L (refill from creek - treating the water is recommended -  or bring extra)
- Clothing: long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day. Electrolytes recommended also.
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.

name: Bullocky Toms Track to Gold Creek Falls
description:
SATURDAY 3 October 2020
 
 REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.
 
 RATED: Hard (on trail but there is elevation gain of 750m)

 DESCRIPTION
 This will be a full day hike on a mountain track. There is a long steep climb, sometimes rough and slippery terrain with uneven footings, tree and rocks roots on track. Some creek crossings are involved (may be slippery rocks). Don't let that scare you off though..... because:

This is a great mountain track walk to a top waterfall and pool. It is a steep climb, ascent of 750 mr. Along the way we'll pass scenic creeks, a great lookout. We'll stop at the beautiful Gold Creek falls at the top and have a swim and a well deserved rest. Return will be by the same route. Note this is in conjunction with the 3 day hikers doing the range traverse (but we will not help carry their heavy packs up the track .... unless you really want to help them 🙂).
 
 FITNESS
 To be suitable for this walk, a good analogy would be doing a Castle Hill spur, without a track, three times with ease before lunchtime.
 
 WHAT TO BRING
 - Water: you will need water for half day eg minimum 2L  and refill from the creeks - treating the water is recommended - or carry enough for the full day.
 - Clothing: there is some long grass and scrub so full long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
 - Enclosed footwear
 - Food for the day
 - Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
 - Usual bushwalking gear 
 - Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.
- Hiking poles - optional but very useful. The descent can be steep and slippery.

name: Paluma Range Traverse (3 days)
description:
The Paluma Range traverse is a fantastic 3 day, 35 km track walk with mountain creeks, lookouts, waterfalls, world heritage wet tropics rainforest, and camping at nice creeks.

WHEN
October Long Weekend 3rd-5 th Saturday to Monday

WALK DESCRIPTION
A fantastic 3 day, 35 km hike to traverse the Paluma Range rainforest tracks system, from Paradise Lagoon (Mutarnee) to Jourama Falls. The route follows rainforest mountain tracks.

Day 1 is a 10 km hike, cross Crystal Creek, pass nice mountain creeks, climb up Bullocky Toms track, via Cloudy Lookout and Gold Ck Falls (top spot!) to camp at Johnstone’s Clearing, a wonderful rainforest camp spot next to a rainforest creek. It is approx an 800 mr ascent. So yes, it is a steep climb up Bullocky Toms Track (2 to 3 hrs continual steep up from Cairn Ck to Gold Ck Falls).

Day 2 is a nice undulating 15 km rainforest walk through the top of the range. But the undulations means still an overall ascent over the day of 450 mr with overall descent is 540 mr – call it flattish then ! Pass through DCK Hut, Mt Spec, Prospector Creek, to camp at Station Creek, adjacent to a rainforest creek.

Day 3 is a wonderful day,  only 11 km, all downhill after the first hour or so, to Waterview Ck. Maybe detour to Black Hole Falls. Then reach the amazing top of Jourama Falls. The finale is to descend the slopes with great views of Jourama Falls as you descend, to reach the car park. Total descent of 1,000 mr (ascent of 300 over the day), there are some steep down bits. Oh, after the top of Jourama Falls, there is a short steep climb though before the finale descent  J

Whilst a track walk, it can be on rough rainforest tracks with tree roots, uneven footing, and rocks at times.

WHAT YOU NEED TO BRING
You need to be self sufficient for 3 days of walking and camping.
- Hiking / Camping gear – keep it light (recommend lightweight shelter (tent/tarp) with insect protection, lightweight mattress and sleeping bag/quilt, cooking gear)
-  Insect repellent
- Sun protections: hat, sunscreen, long sleeve clothing
- Hiking poles will be handy for some walkers.
- Water  – generally only need to carry 2 lt of water during the day, but have capacity for 4 lt. Refill from rainforest creeks (recommend treat / filter water refills). Electrolytes are recommended.
- Camp clothes recommended - include a fleece or something warm for nights (some also take thermals as nights can be chilly). Wet weather gear.
- Food and drinks for 3 days
- Personal first aid kit

Any questions about hiking / camping gear suitability, feel free to ask Wilfred (walk leader)

WHEN
Start: Saturday 3/10 - expect an early start!
Finish: Monday 5/10 - Back at cars approx 5pm

Must be over 18years to participate
